## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (also known under the collective commentary title *Paramatthadīpanī*) is the Theravāda Abhidhamma commentary covering the final five treatises of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Collins 1998; Nyanatusita 2008]. In traditional bibliographies, its individual components are classified sequentially as *Pañca-pakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* I through V, comprising commentaries on the *Dhātukathā* (Part I), *Puggalapaññatti* (Part II), *Kathāvatthu* (Part III), *Yamaka* (Part IV), and *Paṭṭhāna* (including the *Tikapaṭṭhāna*) [Collins 1998; Nyanatusita 2008]. In the Pali scholastic tradition, the work is attributed to the fifth-century commentator Buddhaghosa [Nyanatusita 2008]. Later subcommentarial literature composed on these texts includes the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* (also called *Paramatthapakāsanī*) and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā* [DharmaNexus; Nyanatusita 2008].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive text-reuse connections within the Pali corpus, recording over 85,000 matches across more than 600 texts [DharmaNexus]. The highest volume of internal shared text occurs with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (over 465,000 shared characters), its subcommentaries *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* and *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā*, as well as the canonical *Paṭṭhāna* treatises (notably the *Kusalattika*, *Nikkhepavāra*, and *Mahantaraduka*) and the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with a score of 10 or higher are reported [DharmaNexus].
